title: Tech Note: Building a REST Client
author: Yvan Ayaay, Technical Support Engineer, 4D Inc.

historical_commentary.text: This note explains REST as a then-emerging alternative to SOAP web services and walks through hand-building a REST client in 4D 2004 language, since 4D's Web Services Wizard at the time could only discover and call SOAP services. The core architectural explanation of REST (resource-oriented, stateless, HTTP verbs over URLs) remains entirely accurate and foundational to modern web APIs, but the concrete 4D-side implementation — manual HTTP/XML handling without any REST-specific commands or JSON support — has been superseded by 4D's later native REST/JSON tooling and its own built-in REST server framework (introduced circa 4D v16+).
related_updates: 4D has since added its own native REST server/API framework and JSON parsing commands, eliminating the need to hand-roll REST clients as shown here
The example calls Yahoo's now-discontinued classic Web Search REST API, which is no longer operational
